_comment: DUO-3222/DUO-3227: the ONE project-level WordPress/PHP/database compatibility statement. PHP and database use min-inclusive/max-exclusive ranges. WordPress remains a single last-verified version because no multi-version core matrix exists; the generated capability registry treats any other target version as unproven and blocks a certified verdict. Doctor reports this baseline and the release/registry evaluator is the authoritative product gate -- never independently-maintained numbers.

php.note: Pinned by the sandbox harness's own Docker tags (wordpress:7.0.3-php8.3-apache / wordpress:cli-php8.3 -- see sandbox/pair.yml, sandbox/db.yml, sandbox/docker-compose.yml). Verified live: PHP 8.3.33 as of this writing.

database.note: Pinned by the sandbox harness's own Docker tag (mariadb:11 -- see sandbox/db.yml, sandbox/docker-compose.yml). Verified live: 11.8.8-MariaDB as of this writing. MySQL is not claimed or tested against; a site running MySQL instead of MariaDB is genuinely untested, not merely unpinned.

wordpress.note: Exact evidence boundary, not a claimed range: the sandbox image is not core-version pinned, so only the version recorded by each capability's current subject evidence is certified. Any other target version receives wordpress_version_mismatch until fresh subject evidence updates this value; a wider range requires a real multi-version core matrix.
